value: seedling height growth fell in deep shade: relative growth rate in height (RGRh) of A. negundo was about 13 times higher in full light and 25 percent light (on average) than in 7 percent light under fertilisation, against 1.23 and 1.5 times for the early- and late-successional native trees; the shade effect on A. negundo RGRh was significant (p = 0.0116, shade x fertilisation p = 0.0155), while native growth did not respond significantly to shade
method: greenhouse shade experiment: seedlings under full light (100 percent ambient), shade (25 percent) and deep shade (7 percent), crossed with fertilisation (2 levels) and mechanical disturbance (2 levels); four individuals per species in each of 12 treatments (720 seedlings across five species), split-split-plot design with 3 complete random blocks; relative growth rate in height
conditions: treatments applied 1 April to 14 June 2005; A. negundo seeds collected fall 2003 along the Garonne River and sown spring 2004; the 13-fold figure is for high nutrient availability and averages the full-light and 25 percent treatments; native comparators Fraxinus excelsior, F. angustifolia, Populus nigra, Salix alba; per-species-by-treatment n is 4 seedlings, so the paper's figure means rest on 9 to 12 seedlings per point; the paper gives no separate p value for the fertilised full-light against deep-shade contrast

value: white clover (genotype A120) infected with White clover mosaic virus emitted a volatile blend that separated from mock-inoculated plants (canonical discriminant analysis, p < 0.0001, kappa 0.92); beta-caryophyllene was detected only in the headspace of infected plants; in a separate choice test adult fungus gnats preferred non-infected plants (67 versus 33 percent, p = 0.0278), a link to the volatiles that the authors suggest but did not test directly
method: whole-plant headspace collection (80 min, Tenax TA and Carbopack B traps) from cuttings of four ramets inoculated on the first two fully expanded leaves 4 days earlier, infected against mock-inoculated (buffer only) controls, 13 replicate samplings per treatment, volatiles analysed by GC and canonical discriminant analysis
conditions: single clonal genotype A120; volatile and gnat choice experiments used separate plant sets and different inoculation lead times (4 days for volatiles, 18 and 3 days for choice tests); no volatiles were collected during the choice tests; the same paper reports virus infection cut biomass by 27 percent and gnat larval feeding by 52 percent
